title: Short-video feed
brief: People swipe through an endless feed of clips of 10 to 30 seconds. The next clip must already be on the phone before the swipe. One clip can suddenly get millions of views, and every view is a signal that picks what to show next.

clarify.q: Does the app start loading the next clip early?
clarify.a: Yes. The phone prefetches one or two clips ahead. That means fewer stalls but more data sent per viewer.

clarify.q: Is the feed the same for everybody?
clarify.a: No. Every person gets a ranked list picked just for them from a huge pool of clips.

clarify.q: How soon should a new clip show up?
clarify.a: Within a minute for the creator and their followers. Everyone else can wait a bit.

clarify.q: Can we lose a "like" or a view count?
clarify.a: A few can be late or missing. A posted clip's file sits in object storage, which keeps it safe; at most the last minute of new posts may need posting again after a failure.

notes: A short clip is about 6 MB in total, which the game counts as a few 2 MB chunks (approx.).

hints: One clip can get a huge share of all views for an hour. Where in your design does that clip live?
A CDN holds popular clips so they never reach your servers. Choosing the next clips is a recommender job: it is slow, so keep its answers in a cache and have a fallback if it is slow.
Approximate ranking does not justify unbounded retry amplification; track freshness separately. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: Short-video apps have two jobs with opposite shapes. Delivering the clip is a CDN job: big, identical, cacheable. Choosing the clip is a recommendation job: small, personal, slow, and exactly the part that must not block the swipe. Keep them apart, cache the ranking, and push the signals through a queue.

designs.name: CDN for clips, cached recommender for the feed
designs.why: The CDN keeps the viral clip at the edge. The feed service asks a recommender for a short list, caches it for a short time, and falls back to a popular list if the recommender is slow. Views and likes go through a queue and arrive a little later.

tradeoffs: Prefetching the next clip makes swiping feel instant but sends data the viewer may never watch. That extra bandwidth is a real line on the bill.
Caching the ranked feed for a minute is cheap but makes the feed slightly less fresh. A fresh-for-you feed costs a recommender call on every swipe.
A circuit breaker returns a popular-clips list when the recommender is slow. The feed is a little less personal for a few minutes instead of broken.
Counting views through a queue means view counts lag by seconds. A creator will not mind, but a payout calculation would need a more careful path.
editorial.realWorld: Short-video apps usually prefetch the next one or two clips (approx.). The most viewed clips of the day may account for a large share of all video bytes, which is why edge caches work so well.

correctness.prompt: Short-video feed: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Separate personalized ranking from reusable video and bounded prefetch. Shared media and personalized metadata have different cache scopes. Excess prefetch wastes bandwidth and can delay the clip being watched. Approximate ranking does not justify unbounded retry amplification; track freshness separately.

fields.label: Step 1. Two users request their next feed page. Share a single cache entry?
options: Key personalized ranking by user and feed cursor; reuse immutable clip bytes separately
Cache the full feed only by page number
fields.explanation: Shared media and personalized metadata have different cache scopes.

fields.label: Step 2. A phone has a slow link. How much should it prefetch?
options: A bounded next-clip window adapted to buffer and bandwidth
The next hundred clips to maximize cache hits
fields.explanation: Excess prefetch wastes bandwidth and can delay the clip being watched.

fields.label: Step 3. A view event retries after ranking already consumed it. Count it again?
options: Deduplicate by event id and retain a ranking watermark
Increment every time because aggregate counts are approximate
fields.explanation: Approximate ranking does not justify unbounded retry amplification; track freshness separately.

correctness.responsibility: Separate personalized ranking from reusable video and bounded prefetch.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.
